item.title: A shitbox as a step towards digital sovereignty (Nextcloud setup)
item.description:
Trying to selfhost basic services: attempt 953284753.

Once again did the reality dawn on me. To check my upcoming appointments, I open… Google Calendar. To open one of my prehistoric files I had on a computer I put away in 2017, I open… Google Drive. item.title: This is the best article ever /hj (hopelessness included)
item.description: Tone indicators are definitely among my favourite features of written language used on the internet. During an in-person conversation, the tone of voice, facial expression and overall body language of your conversation partner would (ideally) give away if they’re joking, being sarcastic or something of similar nature. When you lead a conversation on the internet though, it usually takes place in written form – meaning these cues (which might already be difficult to spot for some) get completely lost. Thankfully – given that the writer is enlightened enough to use them – tone indicators come to the rescue and bluntly state (or indicate, if you may), well, the tone of the message. But… are they really as unambiguous as they like to pretend to be? (spoiler alert: no)
